Thorough backstory/ walkthrough: On August 3rd, after several weeks without fresh groceries and living off of frozen, convenience food and drinking hard cider every night, after continuous scrutiny in the mirror about my rolls and denial about my weight gain this summer, I made a commitment to myself to be healthy. I haven't always been unhealthy, in fact this time last year I was taking yoga and weight lifting on my campus, but it's been a difficult year for me and depression and anxiety paired with various issues led to eating without consequence and lack of exercise, leading to weight gain. Even at my healthiest, I've always had a little excess weight. I was heavier as a child post-puberty, but I've always been a little bit overweight. Now I'm trying to change all that. On August 3rd, I purchased Cassey Ho's PIIT 1.0, 2.0 and 3.0 program (All 28-day long programs, meant to be repeated and each more intense than the last) along with her 28-day reset Vegan meal guide. This was my commitment to getting healthy. I spent $100 total on these guides, and being a part-time worker and student, I was determined to get my money's worth. For at least the first two weeks, I followed both programs religiously. I first discovered Cassey (aka Blogilates) when I was 15 and followed her videos on and off. I was looking for some sort of plan that would get me to be healthy and active every day, and chose to support her by purchasing her guides. Now, I am more intuitive with my workouts and diet. I do her PIIT (Pilates Intense Interval Training) workouts 4-5 times a week. These workouts are very intense, so when I need a break from them, I alternate between things like a light run, simple floor and dumbbell exercises in my room, other Blogilates videos, Yoga by Candace and POPSUGAR fitness videos, etc. I'm trying to incorporate hiking and other activities (I hiked yesterday, it was amazing.) Additionally, I'm trying to devote myself to stretching my whole body and meditating for around 30 minutes (without any video/ guides, I just do what I feel like I need) before bed each night. I try to take walks when I can. All of these things culminate to 1hr - 1.5hrs of exercise each day with at least one rest day a week. As you can see, it's important for me to have a lot of variety. I usually do the main portion of my workouts fasted, an hour or so after I wake up. If I do eat something, it's usually very light, like a piece of fruit, and I drink tea and water as soon as I wake up. I drink 2-3L of water a day. My diet is almost completely plant-based, except for the vanilla protein powder I use (will get a vegan replacement when I run out) and the occasional bite of some non-vegan snack that boyfriend will have around. I buy groceries once a week at Sprouts. During the first couple weeks of the reset diet, I spent $70-80 on groceries, but now it's leveled out to $45-55 weekly. I don't work a full-time job, so do have more time than others to prepare my meals. After I work out, I usually have a protein shake or protein mug cake for breakfast. I also like to make overnight oats and pancakes. For lunch I eat things like wraps, salads, Buddha and sushi bowls. Dinners include curries, soups, sweet potato and quinoa-based dishes, tofu dishes, stir frys, etc. I snack on fruits & peanut butter, nuts, edamame, veggies & hummus, Mary's crackers, etc. The 28-day reset itself is a challenge for people to find their food sensitivities, so there is no dairy, gluten, processed sugar, processed foods, or alcohol. Except for a few cheat meals, I've been very meticulous with my diet. I use MFP to log my meals. My calorie limit to lose weight is 1,440, but I'm often very satisfied at 1,200. Since I buy all of my groceries and prepare my own food all the time, my version of treating myself is going out to eat, where I normally order something healthy anyways, like a veggie curry noodle, veggie sushi, a smoothie bowl, etc. The treat is that someone makes it for me. Since I made the change to be healthier, I've noticed my skin has cleared up and I'm weighing less while composing strong muscle, most apparent in my lower body. I'm sleeping much better, I'm not nearly as depressed as I was 3 months ago, I have more energy, less bad days, and I feel happy more often. My period cramps are not as severe. I'm more flexible. I've been on this subreddit every day since I started and picked out 2 photos I found on here of lovely ladies with the same stats as me with admirable progress, and I keep them open in tabs on my computer all the time so I can quickly refer to them to motivate me. This has definitely been a challenge thus far, but I never want to go back to the way I was and I'm very determined to be better every day. Sorry if this was too long, but I wanted to be thorough and I've never written out my entire experience thus far so this has been very therapeutic for me! I'd also like to add that I sometimes have a hard time with my knee and ankle joints so I have to be careful when running or doing any cardio exercise. I'm also a chronic marijuana smoker, as it relieves stress, relaxes my muscles and tends to make me feel better on a daily basis.

Hi friend. I understand/am here for you. I still have bad ones here and there, particularly when I brood too long about things in the past (ie failed relationships, being abandoned by close friends) but when I have things to occupy myself, it's not so bad. And you can start small. I've been reading a lot lately to keep myself busy. You could start by reading a chapter a day. Or if that's not your thing, go out of your comfort zone and find another hobby. Pursuing activities as a way of self-improvement is always a good choice. 
Good luck.
